images.title: More chikkis, same friends
images.purpose: Show that sharing more chikkis among the same 5 friends gives each friend more fifths, so 1/5 < 2/5.
images.composition: Two panels side by side with wide space between them, and one share row centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: one rectangular chikki bar cut into 5 equal pieces; 1 piece filled teal #0072B2, 4 plain. Right panel: two chikki bars of exactly the same size, stacked, each cut into 5 equal pieces; in each bar 1 piece filled amber #E69F00, 4 plain. Below, centred: one friend's share from each panel laid in a row, 1 teal piece then 2 amber pieces joined, all pieces the same size as in the bars; the 2 amber pieces outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 3 bars, 15 pieces, 1 teal, 2 amber, 1 share row.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
chikki bars of different sizes, or pieces that are not equal
images.takeaway: Same friends means the same unit; more chikkis means more of those units each.
images.description: One chikki cut into 5 equal pieces gives each friend 1/5; two such chikkis give each friend one piece from each, 2/5; the share row shows 1/5 < 2/5.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one friend's share in each panel and explain in words why the second share is bigger.

image_decisions.why: The reason, more chikkis among the same friends, is easiest to say while looking at the two panels.
